provisions.text: The citizens shall be entitled without previous permission to form associations for any lawful purpose. Associations employing violence, or aiming at attaining their object by violence, by instigation to violence, or by similar punishable influence on people of other views, shall be dissolved by judgment. No association shall be dissolved by any government measure. However, an association may be temporarily prohibited, provided that proceedings be immediately taken against it for its dissolution. Cases relating to the dissolution of political associations may without special permission be brought before the highest court of justice of the Realm. The legal effects of the dissolution shall be determined by Statute. The citizens shall without previous permission be entitled to assemble unarmed. The police shall be entitled to be present at public meetings. Open-air meetings may be prohibited when it is feared that they may constitute a danger to the public peace. In case of riots the armed forces, unless attacked, may take action only after the crowd in the name of the King and the Law has three times been called upon to disperse, and such warning has been unheeded. Every male person able to carry arms shall be liable with his person to contribute to the defense of his country under such rules as are laid down by Statute. The right of the municipalities to manage their own affairs independently under the supervision of the State shall be laid down by Statute. All privileges by legislation attached to nobility, title, and rank shall be abolished. In future no fiefs, estates tail in laud or estates tail in personal property shall be created. The provisions of sections 71, 78, and 79 shall only be applicable to the defense forces subject to such limitations as are consequential to the provisions of military laws.
